--- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.is_dag()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: Check if directed graph is a DAG (Directed Acyclic Graph). twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.is_dag()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: Check if directed graph is a DAG (Directed Acyclic Graph). title: >- [Graph.is_dag()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Check if directed graph is a DAG (Directed Acyclic Graph). page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Check if directed graph is a DAG (Directed Acyclic Graph). ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L23075-L23184){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.is_dag() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Is DAG](../assets/graphs/is-dag.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Left: a directed graph on five nodes where every edge leads rightward or downward, so no path returns to its start and is_dag() returns True. Right: the same graph with the edge between B and C reversed, which creates the cycle B, E, C, B (shown in the accent color), so is_dag() returns False." width="100%"} A DAG is a directed graph with no directed cycles: there is no way to follow edges in their direction and return to the node you started from. The check runs a depth-first search over the whole graph and reports a cycle as soon as it finds an edge leading back to a node still on the current search path. It takes time linear in the number of nodes plus edges. A self-loop is a cycle of length one, so any self-loop makes the result `False`. The graph doesn't need to be connected, and the current selection is ignored. DAGs model anything with a "must come before" relationship, so this check is useful for: - validating dependency graphs (packages, build targets, task pipelines) before ordering them - confirming that a citation, version, or causal graph has no circular references - guarding calls that require acyclic input, such as `topological_sort()` If the result is `False`, `simple_cycles()` can help locate the offending cycles. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `True` if the graph has no directed cycles, `False` if it contains at least one. A directed graph with no edges is a DAG. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If called on an undirected graph. Note that `ec.Graph()` is undirected by default, so create the graph with `directed=True` to use this method. ::: ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~topological_sort`) : Order the nodes so every edge points forward. [](`~simple_cycles`) : List the directed cycles. [](`~is_arborescence`) : Whether the graph is a directed tree with one root. ## Examples {.doc-examples} A simple chain `A -> B -> C` has no way back to its start, so it is a DAG: ::: {#67311638 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C")]) ) graph.is_dag() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` True ``` ::: ::: Adding an edge back from "C" to "A" closes the loop `A -> B -> C -> A`, so the graph is no longer acyclic: ::: {#17426f29 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.add_edge("C", "A") graph.is_dag() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` False ``` ::: ::: ### A loop in the prerequisites In a course catalog, each edge runs from a course to one that requires it. Because the catalog is a DAG, there's an order in which a student can take every course. Suppose an edit makes Distributed Systems (CS410) a prerequisite for Computer Architecture (CS210), which is itself needed, through Operating Systems and Computer Networks, for CS410. Now no one can take any of the four: ::: {#2c42c6f6 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} catalog = ec.courses().layout_multipartite(subset_key="level") edited = ec.courses().layout_multipartite(subset_key="level") edited.add_edge("CS410", "CS210") loops = [ [edited.get_label_from_id(n) for n in cycle] for cycle in edited.simple_cycles() ] catalog.is_dag(), edited.is_dag(), loops ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` (True, False, [['CS410', 'CS210', 'CS310'], ['CS410', 'CS210', 'CS320']]) ``` ::: ::: The catalog on the left, with the courses in columns by level, and the edited catalog on the right, with the two loops highlighted: ::: {layout-ncol="2"} ::: {#1795ccfe .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} catalog.plot( layout="pos", label_by="label", width=360, height=360, legend=False ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ```{=html}
